production.note: PROVISIONAL. US model years. End: Hagerty: 'After 1999, the model was discontinued in the U.S.' Start: Hagerty's valuation tool lists a 1991 3000 GT VR4 (hagerty-1991-3000gt-vr4); Car Throttle says the car 'debuted in 1990' (carthrottle-3000gt-vr4). No opened page states '1991 model year' in words.

body.note: Hatchback coupe. The 1995-1996 VR-4 Spyder is sold under its own name and is a separate car.

displacementL.note: 'Its 3.0-liter DOHC V-6 featured twin turbochargers and intercoolers'; KBB 'V6, Twin Turbo, 3.0 Liter'. No opened page gave the VR-4's cc figure.

drivetrain.note: 'The VR4 also featured full-time four-wheel drive and four-wheel steering.'

transmission.note: '1994-99 cars also moved from a Getrag 5-speed manual to a 6-speed version of the same gearbox.' 5-speed for 1991-1993. No automatic on the VR-4 (Hagerty: automatics for base/SL models).

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (database and an unsigned article). Quote (KBB 1994 VR-4 Coupe 2D): "Horsepower: 320 @ 6000 RPM". Hagerty: "From 1994-99, this was raised to 320 hp and 315 lb-ft." (hagerty-1994-3000gt). 1991-1993 cars: 'twin turbochargers and intercoolers to produce 300 hp and 307 lb-ft of torque' (Hagerty). Reference year 1994: the 320 hp rating covers six of the nine model years.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (single database). 1994 VR-4 coupe, 6-speed manual (the only transmission). Quote (KBB): "Curb Weight: 3803 lbs." Only one source for the 1994 figure was found. KBB gives 3,759 lb for 1996 and 3,737 lb for 1999 (kbb-1996-3000gt-vr4, kbb-1999-3000gt-vr4); Car Throttle says 'the early VR-4's weighed in around 3800lbs' (approximate).

sources.title: Used Car Buyer's Guide: Mitsubishi 3000GT VR-4

provisionalNote: Power (320 hp) rests on KBB (database) and Hagerty's unsigned valuation text; weight (3,803 lb) rests on KBB alone; the start year 1991 rests on Hagerty's valuation listing. A Mitsubishi Motors America press kit or brochure, or a major magazine spec panel for the 1994 VR-4, would replace them.
